title: Upgrading using silent install does not update all installed powertoys
summary: Command Palette features remain old after a reported silent machine-wide PowerToys upgrade.

judgment.rationale: The silent-upgrade scenario and successful interactive reinstall are reported, but the original version and exact deployment invocation are needed to reproduce it.
evidence: On 0.99.1 the reporter says silent machine-wide upgrades leave new Command Palette features unavailable, while uninstalling and interactively reinstalling restores them.
The report does not include the starting version, deployment command or installed package versions.
The current installer carries the CmdPal MSIX and schedules an impersonated package installation custom action; whether this path explains the report is unknown.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the upgrade version pair, sanitized deployment command and observed Command Palette package version.

fix_assessment.rationale: A package deployment or registration correction may be needed after the failing upgrade path is identified.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate silent upgrade of Command Palette
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a per-user package remains old after a silent machine-wide upgrade; a stale process or configuration is also possible.
plan: Collect the reported upgrade version pair, sanitized command and affected user package version.
Reproduce the same machine-wide transition and compare installed payload, package registration and running process versions with interactive upgrade.
Correct only the established deployment or registration failure, accounting for user scope and restart behavior.
Add focused regression coverage for silent and interactive upgrades across supported install scopes.
verification: The reported version transition gives the affected user the target Command Palette features after normal restart.
Other users and existing installations are not removed or downgraded by the correction.

confidence.rationale: The upgrade symptom is reported but the invocation, initial version and stale component are not established.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette features remain old after a reported silent machine-wide PowerToys upgrade.
known_information: On 0.99.1 the reporter says silent machine-wide upgrades leave new Command Palette features unavailable, while uninstalling and interactively reinstalling restores them.
The report does not include the starting version, deployment command or installed package versions.
inferences: A stale per-user package or another deployment difference could explain the old UI, but neither is established.
initial_investigation: Inspected installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/CmdPal.wxs and Product.wxs: the installer includes an MSIX and has a CmdPal installation custom action.
Reviewed complete thread, no assignee and no timeline fix; searched open PRs for silent CmdPal and issue number without establishing a covering fix.
issue_context.analysis: The exact version transition and deployment command are missing and distinguish package upgrade behavior from a feature setting or stale process. Do not request a generic diagnostic archive before these comparisons.

information_gaps.information: Starting and target PowerToys versions and the sanitized silent installation command or deployment tool context.
information_gaps.why_needed: Recreates the actual upgrade transition and install context.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the version pair, installer name and silent command with any private paths removed.

information_gaps.information: Installed Command Palette package version and which feature is missing after upgrade.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes an old registered package from a configuration or feature-display difference.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: After reproduction, run Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.CommandPalette | Select-Object Name,Version as the affected user, and report the missing feature.

actions.label: Approve silent Command Palette upgrade investigation

comment.body:
Thanks for the report. You noted that reinstalling interactively restored the missing Command Palette features. To compare the silent upgrade path, could you share:
- The starting and target PowerToys versions, installer filename, and silent command or deployment tool used (please remove private paths)?
- After a silent upgrade, the Command Palette package version for the affected user and an example of a missing feature? In PowerShell, run `Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.CommandPalette | Select-Object Name,Version` while signed in as that user.

These details help distinguish an old registered package from a feature or configuration difference.
